clue.text: Dramatist's second work — this classical reading son ignored

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
hoc is Latin, the classical language, for 'this'

indicators.note: ignored says the word son is left out of the reading

parts.note: a lesson is a passage read aloud in church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on a playwright's second piece, read in class with the boy left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' takes SON from LESSON, leaving LES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragedian who wrote Oedipus Rex is a dramatist by profession.

clue.text: Catch son having kiss and cuddle

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A boy is caught smooching his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word, chiefly northern English, for a door latch, i.e. a catch.

clue.text: American hoarder of Sinatra, F and chums, so to speak?

indicators.note: so to speak signals a playful turn of words, here swapping the two halves of the group's name

parts.note: Frank Sinatra and his friends were known as the Rat Pack

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether Sinatra and his friends were Americans who hoarded things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rat Pack's two words swap ends to give the hoarder's name.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a person who collects and keeps useless things is called this, after a rodent that stashes objects.

clue.text: Airport in a bad way — work abandoned after upset

indicators.note: abandoned says the overturned work is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: someone poorly is unwell, in a bad way

indicators.note: upset turns the word for work upside down, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An airport is in a mess, with work left undone after some upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OP into PO; 'abandoned' removes PO from POORLY, leaving the Paris airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris has two main airports, and this one lies south of the city.

clue.text: Naval officer and author having destiny on island

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A sailor-writer whose fate is tied to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Loti was a French naval officer who wrote novels about his voyages.

clue.text: Avant garde type from south-east county, mostly associated with top people

indicators.note: mostly means the county's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Surrey is a county in south-east England
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: An experimental artist from the Home Counties who mixes with the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter of SURREY, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Dalí-style movement of dream imagery were artistic radicals, hence avant-garde.

clue.text: Shift gear initially, entering seaside resort

indicators.note: entering says that letter goes inside the resort's name

parts.note: Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of gear

explanation.surface: Driving into a seaside town, you change gear first.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDE is a surfing resort on the north coast of Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something slightly is to move it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Audible encouragement to William in communication of love?

indicators.note: audible says the phrase is heard, not written, and matches a French term in sound

parts.note: 'Billy, do!' is urging Billy, a pet form of William, to act

explanation.surface: Cheering William on with a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is said roughly 'billy doo' in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A love letter, from the French for 'sweet note', is a romantic message.

clue.text: Mound of food's ending with drink? Nothing turned up

indicators.note: with here means accompanied by, so the drink follows on from the food's last letter
ending picks out the final letter of food's base word

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up reads the word for nothing from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A pile of food finished off with a drink, though none ever showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes D from food; 'turned up' reverses NIL to LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial deposit forming an elongated hill is a kind of mound.

clue.text: Curses river's decrepit transport

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
crates are old, rickety vehicles

explanation.surface: Someone swears at the river's tumbledown vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate someone is to denounce or damn them, so the verbs match as synonyms.

clue.text: Recalculate so as to change part of business contract

indicators.note: to change means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework figures so a contract term alters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges RECALCULATESOAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision allowing prices or wages to rise with costs is a standard contract term.

clue.text: Man of Enterprise in Scottish place of worship

definitions.meaning: Captain James T. ... commands the starship Enterprise in Star Trek
in Scotland a church is called by this name

explanation.surface: A starship crewman spotted in a Scottish church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Trek captain's surname is also the Scots word for church.

clue.text: In Paris I may meet Sam who sells valuable items?

parts.note: je is French for I
Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens

explanation.surface: In Paris I might bump into Sam, a seller of precious things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller is the cheerful manservant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in gems and gold is the trader in valuables described.

clue.text: Like some music that gives backing to R Charles, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way
gives backing reads the word to backwards

explanation.surface: Music that supports the singer Ray Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives backing' turns TO into OT; 'possibly' shuffles OT with RCHARLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for a full symphony band of strings, brass and so on is described this way.

clue.text: University zone, one sealed off very briefly (gosh!) after pub room ceremony

indicators.note: after says the pub room comes first and the rest follows behind it

parts.note: a bar is a room in a pub
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: briefly shortens very to its opening letter
sealed off says the word one is shut out of zone

parts.note: ah is an exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: A university area is cordoned off, followed by a ceremony in a pub function room.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology; the surface reads 'sealed off' as cordoned, but it means a word is shut out of another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish coming-of-age rite for a boy of thirteen is a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Raft we all abandoned — unnavigable part of river?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Everyone leaves the raft at a stretch of river no boat can pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges RAFTWEALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Water dropping over a cliff makes that stretch of the river impossible for boats.

clue.text: Charge forefathers try out in hostile moves

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's charge

indicators.note: out says the word try is removed

parts.note: ancestry is one's line of forebears

explanation.surface: A ward's ancestors attempt aggressive manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes TRY from ANCESTRY, leaving ANCES; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual dances performed before battle are movements made in hostility.

clue.text: Party food — for Americans

parts.note: a do is a party
a nut is a kind of food

explanation.surface: A snack served at parties, spelt the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue: this spelling of the fried ring cake is American.
explanation.definitionFit: The fried ring of sweet dough is party fare, and this short spelling is US usage.

clue.text: Raucous sound of bird

indicators.note: sound of says a word is heard like the bird's name

parts.note: the ruff is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird's harsh, grating call.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, rasping voice can be described as coarse or grating, matching raucous.

clue.text: Nymphs, any number in bras and panties?

indicators.note: in puts the number letter inside the underwear

parts.note: undies are underwear
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: Nymphs, any number of them, in their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Water spirits in folklore are a class of nymph.

clue.text: Something unsightly hiding pretty trees

indicators.note: hiding says the mess surrounds the other word

parts.note: a mess is something untidy and ugly
pretty as an adverb means quite

explanation.surface: An eyesore conceals some attractive trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' is the adverb (pretty good) not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny leguminous shrubs of the American south-west are trees of this kind.

clue.text: One of a number of children sequentially evident in Alcott tale

definitions.text: One of a number of children
definitions.meaning: one of three born at one birth
the words Alcott tale run three Ts together, a set of three in a row

explanation.surface: A child from a large family appears in a Louisa May Alcott story.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Alcott tale' the letters TTT appear consecutively: a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: Three babies born together, or a set of three things, share this name.

clue.text: Classical composer, while avoiding extremes, has place for rock

indicators.note: has means the trimmed composer is joined by the place that follows
avoiding extremes drops the outer letters of the composer's name

parts.note: Handel was a baroque composer
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A composer, staying moderate, finds a spot for rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding extremes' leaves ANDE from HANDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic igneous stone found in the Andes is a type of rock.

clue.text: Back religious believer almost to the end

indicators.note: almost to the end drops the final letter

parts.note: a Hindu is a follower of Hinduism

explanation.surface: Supporting a believer nearly to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, meaning rear, as in rear legs.

clue.text: Female in woods is crazy, showing no feelings for male

indicators.note: for says one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: mad means crazy
dry humour shows no emotion

explanation.surface: A woman in the woods has gone mad, unmoved by any man.
explanation.walkthrough: DRY replaces M in MAD; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree nymph of Greek myth is a female spirit of the forest.

clue.text: Navy limited by unserviceable vessels

indicators.note: limited by says the navy is enclosed by the other abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy is hampered by ships that are out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S, 'unserviceable', is British slang for broken; 'vessels' means containers, not ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Large vases or containers are vessels in the sense of pots.

clue.text: Suggestion inadequate, first to last

indicators.note: first to last moves the opening letter to the end

parts.note: a thin excuse is an inadequate one

explanation.surface: A proposal is weak from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a slight indication or clue, a near-synonym of suggestion.

clue.text: Italian footballer and friend entertaining Tranmere team in a contentious manner

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the club's name inside

parts.note: Bruno Conti was an Italian World Cup winner
Tranmere Rovers is a Merseyside football club
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: An Italian player and his pal host the Tranmere side, stirring up argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Tranmere is an English club from Birkenhead, near Liverpool; Bruno Conti won the 1982 World Cup with Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a way that provokes dispute is behaving controversially.

clue.text: Ropy stuff in clues is allowed, putting a lot off

indicators.note: putting a lot off discards most letters of the phrase, keeping a short run inside

explanation.surface: A setter's complaint that stringy material is allowed in clues, though it puts many off.
explanation.walkthrough: The fibre sits in clueS IS ALlowed; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant fibre used to make cord and twine is rope material.

clue.text: The fellow designated to engage one showed indecision

parts.note: he refers to a fellow

indicators.note: to engage means holding the numeral inside

parts.note: stated means designated or specified
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The man appointed to take someone on dithered.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause through uncertainty is to waver, a direct verb synonym.
